cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the heart is open to what's arriving.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: Keep what you feel near something that draws you unsorted — several reactions at once, none of them picked or ranked.
cells.core:
The light is doing what light does in you — it shows which way without demanding the whole journey yet. You can tell what's drawing you, and you can carry several responses to it at once, and neither crowds the other. That's rarer than it sounds. Most people have to argue themselves into caring about something. You're simply available to it, and the availability is the point.

What keeps this steady is that you don't need any of it to become a decision. Sit with the responses longer than is comfortable — not to build suspense, just to let them stay various. When they settle, they'll settle toward what you actually recognise, rather than the first one that came with a plan attached.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you can't write in, and the openness has gone rigid.
cells.act: bring the directed work to its full standing
cells.ask: Name the smallest real piece of what's ahead, and bring that piece all the way to done today, so it doesn't need you holding it up.
cells.core:
Being open to what's new has turned into being open on a deadline. The readiness is still there, but it's ready the way a door is ready when someone's shoulder is against it — the openness is doing work now. You find yourself finishing feelings before they've arrived, rehearsing the response so no gap is left where something unexpected could land.

Bracing won't get you through; finishing will. Take the smallest real piece of what's ahead and bring it all the way to done — a reply, a decision, one drafted page — and then leave it standing. What's already done can't be pre-lived. The next thing that arrives gets to arrive, instead of being met by a plan you wrote last night.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you, and little reaches you from there.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Find something you began and set down, and take it one step further — just to where it stands a bit larger than it does now.
cells.core:
The pull toward light is somewhere, and it isn't reaching you. You can remember being drawn to something, and the memory doesn't light anything in the present. The openness exists in your history; it just isn't what's running now. You're stood at an entrance that closed a while back, still facing it.

The way back goes through the body, not the feeling. Find something small you began and didn't carry — a draft, a plan, a habit — and move it one step further. Not toward a feeling; toward a form. What was only possible gets to stand at its actual size. The light doesn't need to return first; it returns to someone already moving.

cells.tense: You are writing in a room without knowing it's your own hand on the page.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: Let what comes back to you for what you gave — a thank-you, a hand, a gift — land at full size, without waving it off.
cells.core:
There's a pull in you that others can see, and you keep calling it a mood. You'll say you're just following what interests you this week, and the ones close by are hearing a direction. It's doing its work through your days; your account of it leaves that out entirely.

The whole exchange is where this returns. Receive what comes back when you've given something — a thank-you, an offer, a hand — and don't make it smaller than it is. If someone names what they see in you, let it stand. Fairness runs both ways, and the half that's missing is the receiving. You won't recognise your own direction while refusing the evidence being handed to you.
